14397128.title: File:St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1634092.jpg

ObjectName.value: St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1634092

Categories.value: Taken with Canon PowerShot S3 IS|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Medieval European tiles|Information field template with formatting|Images by Evelyn Simak|Floor tiles in England|Encaustic tiles in the United Kingdom|14th-century encaustic tiles|St Andrew's, Barton Bendish (interior)|Church tiles in Norfolk, England

ImageDescription.value: St Andrew's church - medieval floor tiles. St Andrew's > 1634049 - 1634070 is the only one of three churches in the village which is still in use. St Mary's church > 1634138 - a couple of hundred metres further to the west - became redundant in 1976 and is now in the care of the Churches Conservation Trust. No traces remain of All Saints church > 1634114 which was situated across the road from St Andrew's. Tower and chancel of St Andrew's church were built in the 14th century, whereas the inner doorway > 1634066 dates from around 1200 and shows a merging of Norman and Gothic styles. The porch > 1634065 with its elaborate flushwork, depicting saltire crosses, was added in the 15th century. The church was restored in the 19th century and the stained glass windows > 1634080 date from that time. There are 17th century box pews on the north wall, one of them with the date 1623 carved into the door > 1634089. The simple octagonal baptismal font is C15 > 1634108. Of particular interest is the chancel > 1634076 floor in that it has retained the complete set of original 4 inch square medieval tiles, decorated with varying patterns. And even rarer still is the 14th century piscina > 1634098 with a double drain in the floor below it, which was probably in use during the 13th century when the ritual called for piscinae with two drains. There is no other known example of this combination of two drains in the floor and one in the wall.

14034974.title: File:St Michael's church - Victorian floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1300941.jpg

ObjectName.value: St Michael's church - Victorian floor tiles - geograph.org.uk - 1300941

Categories.value: Taken with Canon PowerShot S3 IS|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Encaustic floor tiles|Decorated tiles|Information field template with formatting|Images by Evelyn Simak|Victorian tiles|Floor tiles in England|Church tiles in England|Ceramic flooring|St Michael's, Ingoldisthorpe (interior)

ImageDescription.value: St Michael's church - Victorian floor tiles. St Michael's church is hemmed in by houses from all sides > 1300902 and difficult to reach. Although its tower can occasionally be glimpsed over roofs and through trees, there is only a narrow driveway > 1300904 and a short section of path leading to it. The churchyard contains a number of interesting old headstones and the remains of an ancient stone cross > 1300916 are situated right in front of the south porch which dates from the 15th century. The main body of the church > 1300908 was built a century earlier and the chancel wall contains lumps of carstone. The church interior > 1300927 was extensively restored by the architect G.E. Pritchett in the mid-19th century. It was during this time that the stained glass was put in many of the windows. According to the Norfolk churches website, St Michael's contains probably the best collection of late 19th and early 20th century glass of any small church in East Anglia > 1300958 - 1300968 - 1300974. Most of the stained glass windows were made in the workshop of the O'Connors and there is work by Robert Bayne and Christopher Webb. The originally square font has been cut at some state to form an octagon, ruining some of the carving > 1301005 - 1301020. The rood screen > 1300931 is also largely original albeit restored and covered with dark varnish. There is a three figure brass > 1301039 on the west tower wall which dates from 1623 and features Agnes Brigge and her parents. This church is kept locked but a key is available on request. http://www.norfolkchurches.co.uk/ingoldisthorpe/ingoldisthorpe.htm

Categories.value: Taken with Canon PowerShot S3 IS|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Encaustic floor tiles|Information field template with formatting|Images by Evelyn Simak|Victorian tiles|Floor tiles in England|Church tiles in England|St Remigius, Roydon, Norfolk (interior)

ImageDescription.value: The church of St Remigius in Roydon - Victorian floor tiles. The church of St Remigius > 1770044 has a round Norman tower with the top section and parapet added in Victorian times > 1770049. Nave and arcade date from the 13th century, the chancel was added a century later. The elaborately carved pulpit > 1770055 is Jacobean and has an hourglass stand attached to it. The church was extensively restored in the 19th century when the south aisle > 1770062 was added. The stained glass > 1770060 dates from that time. What now serves as a vestry on the south side of the chancel is the former medieval south porch.
